newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Mild shakeout seen renewing dlr/mark rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Mild shakeout seen renewing dlr/mark rally.

text.p: Dollar/mark is susceptible to a shallow retreat, as overbought technical conditions unwind, but any short-term pullback should draw buyers ahead of making new highs, analysts said.

"My general bias is to think the dollar is vulnerable to a little bit of corrective price action and that people will be looking to buy the dip," said John Moore, foreign exchange analyst at Technical Data.
According to Moore, the slow stochastics on the hourly dollar/mark chart issued a sell signal on Wednesday.
Additionally, the spread on the moving average convergence-divergence study (MACD) is contracting, suggesting weakness, although it does have a bullish crossover, he said.

"Dollar/mark, in the very short term, is requiring some consolidation at these higher levels to relieve the short-term overbought condition," added Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

Provided the expected pullback holds above chart support in the 1.7090 to 1.7120 area, there remains the potential for the dollar to set a modest new high above the April 28 cycle peak at 1.7389 marks, Spain said.
Dollar/mark could then advance to 1.7475 or so, said Spain, adding: "We look for a rejection of this month's strength from those new highs."
Intraday props are identified at 1.7250/60 and 1.7220, while resistance lies at 1.7325 and 1.7350, said Moore.
The dollar was rebuffed after touching 1.7340 on Tuesday, its highest since May 6.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen is oscillating quietly around 116, analysts said.
Hourly technical studies -- such as parabolics, slow stochastics and moving averages -- all suggest dollar/yen could test short-term support points, said Moore.
Initial support lies around 116 yen, Moore said, followed by 115.60/65 yen.
"While above 115.00 yen, there is short-term potential for a break above 117 and strength to 118.00 to 118.25," Spain added.
But there is very little evidence that an escape from the 115 to 117 dollar/yen range is in the offing soon, Spain said.
